# Lab 3.4: Storage Write API Streaming

## What We Are Going to Do
Stream rows from Python using the Storage Write API's default stream, then change the code to use a committed stream with offsets for exactly-once delivery.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create the target table.**

3. **[CLI] Write rows with the default stream.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">cat &gt; write_default.py &lt;&lt;'EOF'
import os
from google.cloud import bigquery_storage_v1
from google.cloud.bigquery_storage_v1 import types, writer
from google.protobuf import descriptor_pb2
import customer_record_pb2

client = bigquery_storage_v1.BigQueryWriteClient()
parent = client.table_path(os.environ["PROJECT_ID"], "lab03", "stream_events")

template = types.AppendRowsRequest(write_stream=f"{parent}/streams/_default")
descriptor = descriptor_pb2.DescriptorProto()
customer_record_pb2.CustomerRecord.DESCRIPTOR.CopyToProto(descriptor)
template.proto_rows = types.AppendRowsRequest.ProtoData(
    writer_schema=types.ProtoSchema(proto_descriptor=descriptor))
stream = writer.AppendRowsStream(client, template)

rows = types.ProtoRows()
for i in range(1, 6):
    rows.serialized_rows.append(
        customer_record_pb2.CustomerRecord(row_num=i, customer_name=f"cust-{i}").SerializeToString())
request = types.AppendRowsRequest(proto_rows=types.AppendRowsRequest.ProtoData(rows=rows))
print(stream.send(request).result())
stream.close()
EOF
python3 write_default.py</span>
</code></pre>
</div>

5. **[CLI] Switch to a committed stream with offsets.** Change the stream setup in a copy of the script:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">sed -e 's|template = types.AppendRowsRequest(write_stream=f"{parent}/streams/_default")|ws = client.create_write_stream(parent=parent, write_stream=types.WriteStream(type_=types.WriteStream.Type.COMMITTED))\ntemplate = types.AppendRowsRequest(write_stream=ws.name)|' \
    -e 's|request = types.AppendRowsRequest(proto_rows|request = types.AppendRowsRequest(offset=0, proto_rows|' \
    -e 's|range(1, 6)|range(101, 106)|' write_default.py &gt; write_committed.py
python3 write_committed.py
python3 write_committed.py</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The second run fails with an **ALREADY_EXISTS / offset** error. Offsets stop the same rows from being written twice.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Default stream | Rows visible at once, at-least-once |
| Committed stream + offsets | Exactly-once, duplicate write rejected |
| Table | Rows 1–5 and 101–105, no duplicates |
| Format | Protocol buffers |
